_status: RETRACTED — wrong object identified. Not a calibration sample. Closed direction.
_retraction_note: The earlier automated pass (logged 2026-06-10 ~17:18) mis-identified the pieces in these photos as flat translucent 'magnetic building tiles' and processed them as a backlit chit calibration drop. That is WRONG. The pieces are actual Icehouse / Looney Pyramids: small translucent NESTING PYRAMIDS in three sizes, standing point-up. They are 3D, not flat chits. Muhammad caught the misread and confirmed the correction 2026-06-10.

_why_void_not_just_corrected.form_factor: Standing 3D pyramids read from above as a small bright point-up footprint, NOT a uniform flat color field. Chroma photo-scores flat regions from above, so the per-piece mean-RGB 'base' readings below do not represent what Chroma actually samples.
_why_void_not_just_corrected.overlap_was_a_nesting: id 1 ('yellow-over-orange OVERLAP') was NOT a flat partial overlap. It was two same-axis pyramids NESTED/stacked vertically. Chroma's subtractive blend depends on FLAT chits PARTIALLY overlapping so the overlap zone mixes. Vertical nesting does not produce that geometry, so this is not a valid mix data point.
_why_void_not_just_corrected.calibration_invalid: Because both the base geometry and the single 'mix' are wrong for Chroma, the whole thing cannot serve as a Chroma calibration sample. The numbers are not promoted, not interim, not held — they are void for Chroma.

_decision: Icehouse / Looney Pyramids: EVALUATED AND REJECTED as a Chroma chit. Reason: wrong form factor — standing 3D, vertical nesting, no flat partial-overlap blend. Not canon. Just a closed direction.
_what_carries_forward: The translucency + subtractive color instinct is genuinely right. The real Chroma chit still wants FLAT, frameless, uniform translucent pieces that PARTIALLY OVERLAP to blend. That remains the component search direction. See [[project-chroma]].
_also: An even earlier automated pass mis-read these same photos as a calibration drop with 'no red, two blues'. That palette read was an artifact of the same misidentification and is likewise void. Disregard.
_canon_untouched: Design doc (chroma.md), draw-table, and all canonical game data were NOT modified by the bad pass and are NOT modified by this retraction. Nothing here ever reached canon.

_raw_pixel_readings_preserved_for_audit_._note: Retained ONLY as a record of what the bad pass measured. NOT a calibration sample. Do not use for Chroma color modeling — wrong object, wrong geometry.

pieces.described_as: yellow-over-orange (claimed OVERLAP — actually a vertical pyramid nesting)
